full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ : This appeal by leave is from judgment and order dated 25 March 1998 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1259 of 1998 filed by (accused) respondent No. 1 under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure setting at liberty the victim girl Lata Rani Saha alias Jannatul Ferdous from safe custody in the District Jail, Narayangonj saying "she may go anywhere she likes. " 

 2. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the appellant Jharna Rani Saha, as informant lodged a written ejahar with Sadar Police Station District Narayangonj on 12-8-97 implicating accused respondent No. 1 co-accused Masud, Liton and Ismail Hossain in the commission of the offence of abducting her minor daughter Lata Rani Saha, with intention to marry against her will giving rise to Narayangonj Police Station Case No. 1 dated 12-8-97 under section (Kha) and 9 (Ga) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. 

 3. The case was registered as GR Case No. 892 of 1997 and during investigation, the victim girl Lata Rani Saha and accused respondent No. 1 Khondaker Zayedul Hoque were arrested by the police and produced before the learned Magistrate, Narayangonj on 6-10-97. The statement of the victim was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and she was remanded to Jail (safe) custody. 

 7. The father of the victim girl filed an application on 4-1-98 for ascertaining the actual age of the girl by fresh medical examination arid the learned Magistrate having allowed the said prayer by his order dated 22-1-98 respondent No. 1 moved the learned Sessions Judges in revision against the said order, who allowing the revision case, by his order dated 25-2-98 cancelled the Jimma of the girl and put her in the judicial custody for the sake of smooth investigation observing that further examination of the girl was not necessary and that the question of her custody will be considered after' submission of the police report on conclusion of investigation. 

 9. The informant-appellant was not made a party in the High Court Division and the learned Judges in the course of hearing of the Misc. Case directed on 19-3-98 for serving a notice upon the appellant and the matter was adjourned to 25-3-98. 

 10. The appellant has alleged that notice was served upon her at about 11 O'clock on 24-3-98 and she could not take steps for representing herself in the High Court Division due to want of time. The appellant has further alleged that the impugned order was passed ex parte without giving her a reasonable opportunity to submit her case. The girl was set at liberty on 22-4-98 in pursuance of the order of the High Court Division in spite of the order of stay of the impugned order passed by this Division on 1-4-98 which was communicated to the Personal Assistant of the Deputy Commissioner, Narayangonj on 2-4-98 by the father of girl. However, while granting leave to appeal on 3rd June, 1998 the accused-respondent was directed to restore the girl to the Judicial Custody from where she was released and it is reported that the order has been complied with. 

 12. It appears from the impugned judgment that the High Court Division without considering the relevant facts and circumstance of the case, particularly the fact that the appellant mother has alleged that her minor daughter was abducted by the accused and the Case was under police investigation, passed the impugned order of release of the girl merely upon the opinion of the Radiologist that she would be 17/18 years and further upon. Its own (expert) opinion of the X-ray report that "Lata Rani is about to attain the age of 18 years." The case has been dealt with as if the detention of an adult person in Jail Custody was the only matter for consideration for the court. The respondent who was the petitioner before the High Court Division was being accused of an offence under the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain 1995 and the question of age of the victim is not material under the said Act. The girl was put into Jail (safe) custody in the usual manner pending police investigation after her recovery from the accused and the learned Sessions Judge clearly said in his order that the question of her custody will be considered after the submission of the police report. The learned Magistrate was clearly wrong in subsequently giving the girl in the Jimma of the father of the accused which order has been rightly set aside by the learned Sessions Judge. 

 13. It is true that the case of the accused is that the girl is above 18 years of age, she left her father's house on her own and that she voluntarily embraced Islam and married the accused. On the other hand, the guardians allege that she is a minor and the ace used had committed offences under the aforesaid Act. It was totally wrong on the part of the High Court Division not to take into account all these facts and the law itself and to make an order of release upon its own expert opinion that she is about to attain the age of 18 years." 

 18. The whole matter will be decided upon evidence at the trial. But it will be inhuman to keep the girl in the Jail Custody indefinitely. Whether she is Lata Rani Saha or Zannatul Ferdous, her welfare demands that she should be allowed to come out of the unwholesome environment of a prison house. She has already been there for about 9/10 months and it is uncertain when the trial will conclude. Having regard to the facts and circumstances as noticed above and the law under which the accused is being prosecuted, we think it is right and proper that the girl should stay with her parents rather than be given to the family of the accused. The girl cannot be allowed to make her own choice because, prima facie, it appears that she is a minor. The defence can call her as a witness at the trial and the Court will ensure her attendance in that case. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed. Let the girl Lata Rani Saha now detained in District Jail, Narayangonj in connection with Narayangonj PS Case No. 16 dated 12-8-97 and, GR Case No. 892 of 1997 be released and put in the custody of her mother, appellant Jharna Rani Saha forthwith.
